meta.notice: Static assessment only. Findings are indicators for authorized review, not proof of exploitability in a deployed environment.

findings.title: minimist: prototype pollution via crafted CLI arguments
findings.impact: This application pins minimist 1.2.5, which is affected by CVE-2021-44906 (minimist: prototype pollution via crafted CLI arguments). Public technical details and exploit tooling exist for this vulnerability; internet-wide scanners actively probe for it. A known-vulnerable dependency converts an unknown risk into a scheduled one.
findings.remediation: Upgrade minimist to 1.2.6 or later, re-run the dependency audit, and add automated dependency monitoring (e.g. Dependabot/Renovate) so pinned versions cannot silently age into known-vulnerable releases.

findings.title: Dynamic code evaluation (eval / Function constructor)
findings.impact: If any part of the evaluated string is influenced by a request, an attacker achieves remote code execution with the full privileges of the application process — complete server compromise, not just data exposure.
findings.remediation: Remove eval/Function entirely. Replace dynamic behavior with lookup tables, configuration, or a vetted templating engine that does not execute code.

findings.title: SQL query built by string concatenation (SQL injection)
findings.evidence: const query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '" + username +
findings.impact: An unauthenticated attacker can manipulate the query through normal input fields to bypass authentication and read or modify the entire database. In a system holding patient records this is a reportable data-breach scenario and the most commonly exploited web flaw in healthcare breaches.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements everywhere (never interpolate input into SQL text). Add a least-privilege database account and automated regression tests with injection payloads.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret committed to source code
findings.impact: The secret is exposed to everyone who has ever had repository access — employees, contractors, backups, and any future repo leak. Rotation is the only remedy once committed, and abuse (e.g. of a billing key) is billed to you.
findings.remediation: Rotate the exposed credential immediately, then move secrets to environment variables or a secrets manager. Scrub git history and add pre-commit secret scanning.

findings.title: Weak hash (MD5/SHA1) protecting passwords or sensitive data
findings.impact: MD5 and SHA1 are fast hashes: a single consumer GPU tests billions of candidates per second. If the credential store is ever exposed, effectively every password falls within hours, and users reuse those passwords elsewhere.
findings.remediation: Rehash passwords with a password-specific KDF (bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2id) with per-user salts. Force a password reset on next login for existing accounts.

findings.title: No HTTP security headers configured
findings.impact: Without headers such as Content-Security-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options, the application is exposed to clickjacking, MIME-confusion, and easier cross-site scripting exploitation — low-effort attacks that automated tooling attempts against every site.
findings.remediation: Add a hardened header set (helmet for Express, or explicit response headers) including Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and frame protections; verify with a response-header scan.

findings.title: Verbose error output leaks stack traces / internals
findings.evidence: send(res, 500, JSON.stringify({ error: err.message, stack: err.stack, query }), 'application/json');
findings.impact: Stack traces and raw queries hand attackers a map of the codebase — file paths, library versions, table and column names — dramatically shortening the time needed to craft a working exploit against the other flaws present.
findings.remediation: Return generic error messages to clients; log full detail server-side only. Ensure NODE_ENV=production error handling is enforced and covered by a test that forces an exception.
